data.body_html:
February in Marbella offers a rare blend of mild Mediterranean winter weather and uncrowded seas, making it an ideal month for an off-peak boat charter. While summer crowds have vanished, the Costa del Sol still delivers 13-18°C air temperatures, around 6 hours of daily sunshine, and calm seas perfect for coastal cruising. Our fleet departs exclusively from Puerto Banús, and with off-peak pricing starting at €749 for a 2-hour charter on the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39, February presents a budget-friendly window to explore Marbella's coastline by boat.

February Weather in Marbella: What to Expect

February is one of Marbella's cooler months, but it remains mild compared to northern Europe. Average daytime highs reach 18°C, with overnight lows around 8°C. Sea temperatures hover at 15°C, which is too cool for prolonged swimming without a wetsuit, but perfect for sightseeing. The prevailing wind is light, typically 5-15 knots from the west, though occasional Levante easterlies can bring a few days of stronger breezes. Rain is infrequent — February sees only 4-6 rainy days on average. For the most accurate forecasts, check Marbella boat rental conditions before your trip.

Best Boats for February Chartering

For cooler days, enclosed or flybridge boats provide comfort and panoramic views. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers a heated saloon and outdoor deck space. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) includes a free jet ski and spacious interior. Smaller groups may prefer the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) for a cosy, affordable trip. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance — no hidden extras.

Pricing and Availability in February

February is low season, so availability is high and prices are at their most competitive. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full 8-hour day. Tier B boats (Mangusta 80 variants) start at €4,719 for a 4-hour charter, which includes a free jet ski. For other boats like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86, pricing is available on request via WhatsApp. All prices include Spanish IVA (21%).

What to Wear and Bring

Layering is essential: a thermal base layer, fleece or jumper, and a windproof jacket. Sunglasses and high-SPF sunscreen are still necessary due to UV reflection off the water. Non-slip shoes are recommended. The boat provides blankets, and the cabin is heated. Bring a camera for the stunning views of La Concha and the Marbella coastline.

Suggested February Itineraries

A 2-hour charter from Puerto Banús can take you east towards Marbella Marina and the Golden Mile, or west to Cala del Faro. For a longer trip, a 4-hour charter allows time to reach Cabopino or Estepona, with stops at sheltered coves like Cala Cortés. Full-day charters (8 hours) can extend to Sotogrande or even Gibraltar on calm days.
